svg.title: From an idea to merged tickets
svg.desc: Three Claude sessions. Session 1 settles the behaviour, writes the spec and opens a parent issue and a spec PR. Session 2 breaks the parent issue into sub-issues with blocking links. Session 3 runs Foreman, which takes each unblocked sub-issue through a test writer, the intent judge, an implementer, the mutant writer and a standards reviewer, then opens a PR for you to merge.
svg.text: From an idea to merged tickets
Each panel is one Claude session. The numbers on the arrows match the handoffs in the table.
Every skill and teammate lives in this repo. Where one starts from Matt Pocock's skills, we copy what we need and make it ours.
On GitHub or in the repo
Produces a parent issue, and a spec PR whose new scenarios are proposed but not built
You decide the behaviour, by commenting on the doc until you agree it
Produces a slice map and sub-issues on the parent issue, joined by native blocking links
You decide the slices and their order, from the map, before anything is created
Session 3 · foreman · one pipeline per sub-issue, unblocked ones in parallel
Foreman picks every unblocked sub-issue and gives each step a fresh teammate
Produces one PR per sub-issue, carrying the implementer's evidence that it verified the change
You decide whether each PR merges. The parent issue closes with its last sub-issue, once any decision that should outlast it is in docs/adr
Teammates test writer, intent judge, implementer, mutant writer, standards reviewer. Only the intent judge and mutant writer exist today
You and Claude settle the behaviour by grilling it
write-spec takes what you settled and drafts the spec
The draft is a shared Claude doc: you comment on it and write-spec revises it until you agree it
Once agreed, the doc becomes specs/…/spec.md, with a test.todo for each new scenario
The spec change goes up as a PR, its new scenarios proposed but not built
The parent issue says why the change is happening, and links the spec PR and its scenario IDs
to-tickets reads the parent issue and the scenarios it links
to-tickets draws a slice map: the vertical slices, what each adds to the system, and the order they land in
You review the map; anything you'd merge, split or reorder goes back to to-tickets
Once you approve, the map goes on the parent issue and each slice becomes a sub-issue with native blocking links
The test writer turns the ticket's test.todo entries into failing tests
Once the intent judge finds the tests aligned, a fresh implementer makes them pass and records how it verified that
The mutant writer checks the tests fail when the new code is broken; surviving mutants go back to the test writer
The standards reviewer checks the code against CODING-STANDARDS.md; anything off goes back to the implementer
The PR closes its sub-issue with "Closes #N" and carries the verification evidence
You review and merge it; the parent issue closes once its last sub-issue does
